subject: NimbleEdge activation — COI, W-9, and subcontractor declaration needed

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: NimbleEdge activation — COI, W-9, and subcontractor declaration needed

Hi Andrew / NimbleEdge contracting team,

Thanks for choosing Redwood — excited to get NimbleEdge activated so your integration work can start. Before we can issue a PO and route first invoices, procurement needs the following vendor onboarding items:

- Certificate of Insurance (COI) naming Redwood Inference as additionally insured and showing general liability with at least $1M per occurrence and waiver of subrogation where applicable.
- Endorsement page or specific wording on the COI that references "Redwood Inference, its officers, employees and agents" as additional insured.
- Completed W-9 (for US entities) or equivalent tax form.
- Subcontractor declaration: short form confirming whether NimbleEdge will use any third-party subcontractors for Redwood work and the name/controls of those suppliers.
- Billing contact for PO and invoice routing (name, email, remit address).

If you can attach the COI and W-9 in reply that will expedite review. If the endorsement is issued by your broker separately, a PDF of that endorsement or an email from the broker with the required language also works.

We keep activation holds brief — once procurement confirms paperwork we’ll issue a conditional PO and finance will enable invoice routing. Let me know if you need a template for the subcontractor declaration.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Procurement Manager | Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood.com
(415) 555-0172

Diego —

Appreciate the checklist. Attached are the COI and W-9 from our broker and accounting team. Quick notes:

- COI shows general liability and professional liability limits per our policy. The endorsement page is being issued by our broker and will land separately early next week.
- W-9 is completed and attached.
- On subcontractors: we do plan to use a single named subvendor (EdgeOps LLC) for managed deployment work. I’ve attached a short declaration document that lists the subcontractor and confirms we carry oversight controls.

Attachments: NimbleEdge_Certificate_of_Insurance.pdf; NimbleEdge_W9.pdf; Subcontractor_Declaration.pdf

Happy to jump on a quick call with procurement if you want broker contact details or to walk through the endorsement timing.

Thanks,

- COI shows required limits but endorsement page not yet attached. Broker has confirmed it will follow by 2027-04-27. Do we accept the COI conditionally and issue a provisional PO pending endorsement?
- Subcontractor_Declaration lists EdgeOps LLC as a named subvendor; declaration describes security controls but not full SOC2 evidence. Do we need an additional questionnaire for EdgeOps or is the declaration sufficient for a conditional activation?

Thanks Diego — I reviewed the COI and W-9. Finance (Sean) and I are okay to move forward with a conditional PO under these stipulations:

- Issue a provisional PO with "activation contingent on receipt of endorsement" and set a 14-day window for the endorsement to be uploaded to the vendor file (target 2027-05-12).
- Require NimbleEdge to submit EdgeOps' subcontractor evidence (summary controls + point of contact). If EdgeOps cannot provide a SOC2 report we will accept a scoped questionnaire and encrypted data handling attestation.
- Accept net-30 payment terms; Sean will create PO to reflect that and the remit-to address on the W-9.

Karthik — if legal wants to weigh in on the subcontractor wording I can hold issuance until we have your clearance, otherwise I’ll issue the provisional PO today and set tasks for vendor follow-up.
